newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Brembo Q1 1997 turnover up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Brembo Q1 1997 turnover up 15 pct.

text.p: Italian automotive brake maker Brembo SpA saw first quarter 1997 turnover rise 15 percent, the same rise forecast for the whole year, investor relations manager Roberto Vavassori said on Wednesday.
He told a news conference the company confirmed forecasts made earlier this month for a similar rise in 1997 sales to 430 billion lire "barring major and for now unforeseen disruptions."
Group earnings before interest and tax this year would be around 10.5 percent of turnover and net profit some six percent of turnover, he said.
"The way the first quarter has gone is in line with full-year forecasts," he added.

He said that of the 40 percent of Brembo capital floated on the Milan stock market in July 1995, five-sevenths was in the hands of Italian investors with the rest held by major institutional investors.
At 1242 GMT, Brembo shares were quoted up 0.33 percent at 17,400 lire on a generally firmer market.
Brembo last month announced 1996 consolidated net profit fell to 19.1 billion lire from a previous 30.1 billion on higher sales of 357.4 billion lire against 331.2 billion.
